clue.text: Philosopher 'in decrepit aircraft putting out appeal for help

indicators.note: the decrepit aircraft sits in the middle of the distress call, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
a crate is slang for an old, rickety aeroplane

explanation.surface: A thinker aboard a clapped-out plane sends out a distress call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CRATE inside SOS; 'putting out' just describes the call being sent. The stray mark before 'in' is a speck on the newsprint.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian thinker who questioned everyone is the archetypal ancient sage.

clue.text: Heavenly music-maker all round

definitions.meaning: the celestial globes thought by ancient astronomers to hum the music of the heavens
a ball shape is round in every direction

explanation.surface: A celestial musician who is round in all respects.
explanation.definitionFit: First: one of the crystal shells of Ptolemaic astronomy making celestial music; second: a perfectly round solid globe.

clue.text: Scar shown by a critic injured in the middle of a scene

indicators.note: injured suggests damaged and bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged
take the central letters of the run of letters in the words given

explanation.surface: A critic hurt midway through a play scene shows a scar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges A CRITIC to CICATRI; 'in the middle of' takes CE, the centre of ASCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical word for the mark left by a healed wound.

clue.text: What can be the matter with Keat's knight at arms?

definitions.text: What can be the matter with Keat's knight at arms?

parts.words: What can be the matter with Keat's knight at arms?
parts.note: Keats's 'La Belle Dame sans Merci' opens: 'O what can ail thee, knight-at-arms'

explanation.surface: Asking what is wrong with the knight in Keats's ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: The ballad's question 'what can ail thee' suggests the noun for what ails you, an illness. 'Keat's' is the setter's spelling of Keats's.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorder or illness: what ails a person.

clue.text: Journalist's support for Mrs Browning initially declined

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits beneath, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: Elizabeth Barrett Browning's initials are E B B
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist's backing for the poet Elizabeth Barrett Browning faded at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' here means her initials, not the first letter of the clue words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebbed means fell away or receded, like a tide going out.

clue.text: Calculator shows a vehicle holds a hundred

indicators.note: the vehicle holds the second piece, so it is placed inside the vehicle's word

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A bus is reported to be carrying a hundred people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts A C (a hundred) inside BUS, after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads slid along wires, used for reckoning sums since ancient times.

clue.text: Weapon used by some at Sir John Moore's burial (Wolfe)

definitions.text: Weapon used by some at Sir John Moore's burial (Wolfe)

parts.words: Weapon used by some at Sir John Moore's burial (Wolfe)
parts.note: Charles Wolfe's poem on Moore's burial has the soldiers digging 'the sods with our ... turning'

explanation.surface: The arms carried at a general's battlefield funeral, as in a poem by Wolfe.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'The Burial of Sir John Moore after Corunna' the grave is dug with soldiers' blades fixed on muskets.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade fixed to a rifle's muzzle, which Wolfe's soldiers used to turn the turf.

clue.text: Right type, Heather — what a peach!

parts.note: C, Conservative, stands for the political right
ling is the common heather of moorland

explanation.surface: Someone praises Heather as just the right sort: a real peach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type' points to the answer being a variety: a cling is a peach whose flesh clings to the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Clingstone is a variety of fruit whose flesh sticks to the stone.

clue.text: Various items the source of heat dehydrates

parts.note: the sun is the source of the Earth's heat
to dehydrate is to dry out

explanation.surface: Heat from the sun dries out assorted things.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscellaneous small articles too minor to list separately.

clue.text: Danger for climbers the Vicar of Bray (?) found in church

indicators.note: the two pieces are discovered inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
an ass is a donkey, the animal that brays

explanation.surface: The turncoat cleric of the old song in church, a peril to mountaineers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray is a song about a cleric who changed faith with each monarch; here the vicar gives REV and 'Bray' an ASS, with the question mark owning up. 'found in' puts REVASS inside CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep crack in a glacier, a hazard to mountaineers.

clue.text: Young American hero brings fruit to a European

parts.note: the huckleberry is a dark American berry
a Finn is a native of Finland

explanation.surface: A boy hero hands a piece of fruit to someone from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's boy narrator, who rafts down the Mississippi with Jim, is a classic juvenile protagonist.

clue.text: Again go over study that includes origins of the Roman Empire

indicators.note: the study word takes the three initials inside it

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it, as at university

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so take the first letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Revising a study that covers the beginnings of the Roman Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts TRE (initials of 'the Roman Empire') inside READ.
explanation.definitionFit: To read something a second time is to cover the same ground once more.

clue.text: US General Joe's contribution to the Walrus's feast?

definitions.meaning: the first name of the nickname of US General Joseph Stilwell
a sour condiment named in Carroll's poem for the oyster supper

explanation.surface: An American general's offering at a fictional walrus's banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: General Joseph Stilwell was nicknamed 'Vinegar Joe'. In Lewis Carroll's 'The Walrus and the Carpenter' the oysters are eaten with 'pepper and vinegar besides'.
explanation.definitionFit: First: the general's nickname word; second: the condiment the Walrus lists for eating oysters in Carroll's poem.

clue.text: Has she a lesson to teach her love?

definitions.text: Has she a lesson to teach her love?

parts.words: Has she a lesson to teach her love?
parts.note: a schoolteacher woman giving a lesson, or a man's kept lover with lessons of a different sort

explanation.surface: A woman with something to teach the man she loves.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both a female schoolteacher and a man's illicit lover; the clue plays on both.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman teacher at a school, or a woman in an extramarital affair, both go by this title.

clue.text: "Life… Stains the white radiance of ____" (Shelley)

definitions.text: Life… Stains the white radiance of ____" (Shelley)

parts.words: Life… Stains the white radiance of ____" (Shelley)
parts.note: a line from Shelley's elegy 'Adonais': life like a dome of many-coloured glass stains the white radiance

explanation.surface: A gap-fill from Shelley's lament for Keats.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blank from the quotation 'Life, like a dome of many-coloured glass, Stains the white radiance of ...' in 'Adonais'.
explanation.definitionFit: The endless time beyond life, whose pure light mortal existence colours, in Shelley's image.

clue.text: Head, of the 'painter, for instance, in a figure of speech

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here of the word that follows

parts.note: a painter is a rope tying up a boat's bow

explanation.surface: A head painted by an artist, described in figurative language.
explanation.walkthrough: A painter in sailing is the line used to moor a small boat, not an artist. The stray marks are newsprint specks.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetorical device such as metaphor or irony, using words beyond their literal sense.

clue.text: Cockney clock-maker is a man of the mountains

indicators.note: London Cockney speech drops the initial aitch

parts.note: a horologist makes clocks and watches

explanation.surface: An East End watchmaker turns out to be a mountain man.
explanation.walkthrough: An orologist studies mountains; the H-less pronunciation of a London Cockney turns one expert into the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar who studies mountain ranges and their formation.

clue.text: Heaven-sent attraction one's mother pursues daily

indicators.note: the later pieces chase after the cleaning lady, so they come behind her

parts.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day
one's read as one is: I plus S
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone's mother chases the cleaning lady, who has a divine magnetism.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma originally meant a divinely given grace, now a compelling personal magnetism.

clue.text: One heard greeting a girl with his beastly laugh

indicators.note: the greeting and the girl's name are listened to, not read, giving the sound of the entry

parts.note: hi is a casual hello; Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone who greets a girl with an animal-like cackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is defined further by 'with his beastly laugh': the animal known for its laughing call.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a single creature, characterised by its laughing call.

clue.text: Fatty's attitude after mountain-climbing near Troy

indicators.note: the attitude piece is placed after the other
in a down entry climbing means going upward, so the mountain's name is read bottom to top

parts.note: Mount Ida is the mountain near Troy
a pose is a bodily attitude or stance

explanation.surface: A stout person's stance after scaling a mountain close to Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns IDA (the mountain near Troy) to ADI; 'near Troy' tells which mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose tissue is the body's fat-storing tissue.

clue.text: Aerodynamic 'control of lift

definitions.meaning: the hinged surface on an aircraft's tailplane that sets its pitch
the American word for a cage carrying people between floors

explanation.surface: An aircraft's control surface governing lift.
explanation.definitionFit: First: a tail flap that raises or lowers an aircraft's nose; second: the US term for a passenger hoist in a building.

clue.text: Sailor has a sole or other seafood

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
sole means only or single, alone

explanation.surface: A sailor has sole or another kind of fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like the flatfish but means single.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sea snail eaten as a delicacy, also called ormer.

clue.text: Clan leader 'in Highland garb appears calm

indicators.note: the leader goes in the garment word

parts.note: a plaid is a tartan cloth worn in Scotland

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter of the word named

explanation.surface: A Scottish chief in tartan looks serene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C (Clan's first letter) inside PLAID. Stray marks are newsprint specks.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means peaceful and untroubled.

clue.text: Bird boy's a hooligan

parts.note: a ruff is a wading bird
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad who watches birds turns out to be a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent, lawless person, a rough or thug.

clue.text: RAF unit loses fifty in the battle

indicators.note: the unit drops the letter for fifty

parts.note: a flight is a small unit of aircraft in the Royal Air Force
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An air force squadron suffers fifty losses in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight is a combat or struggle between forces.

clue.text: Observe the sporting misdemeanour, say, of this bird.

indicators.note: say asks for the phrase to be spoken, giving the sound of the entry

parts.note: see a foul: watch an infringement in a game

explanation.surface: A spectator spots a foul in a match, by way of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the sporting misdemeanour' gives A FOUL, the article becoming 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull, tern or other bird that lives at sea is a marine bird.

clue.text: The gloss he endorsed apparently

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'The gloss he endorsed apparently': SEEN (endorsed) plus HE gives six letters, not SHEEN; no parse found that uses every word once with a fair indicator

clue.text: The scales for instance that may control one's destiny

definitions.meaning: Libra, the Scales, is one of the twelve astrological divisions
astrologers hold that the stars one is born under shape one's fate

explanation.surface: Weighing scales as something that may rule a person's fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, represented by scales, is an astrological star group believed by horoscope readers to influence fate.

clue.text: The song of joy the man's composed

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A joyous song that a man has written.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn or rousing song of praise or celebration.

clue.text: Clothed as, Trojans' were.. by Greeks

definitions.meaning: dressed, as in robes of office
besieged: the Greeks laid siege to Troy for ten years

explanation.surface: How the defenders of Troy were dressed by the Greek army.
explanation.definitionFit: First: formally robed or dressed; second: surrounded by a besieging force.
